author: Rahul kp
title: Labour
simple_words: Labour variance = standard labour cost for actual output minus actual labour cost. Split it into rate and hours effects.

definitions.meaning: Standard cost of labour for actual output minus actual cost of labour paid. Positive is Favourable, negative is Adverse.
Standard rate multiplied by idle hours paid but not worked. It is always Adverse.

key_points: ==Labour Rate Variance== arises from paying a different rate per hour than standard.
==Labour Efficiency Variance== arises from actual hours worked differing from standard hours for actual output.
Idle time hours are paid but not worked, so they are !!excluded from efficiency!! and shown separately.
Mix and yield variances split efficiency when workers of different grades are used.

formulas.name: Labour Rate Variance
formulas.legend: AH paid = actual hours paid, SR = standard rate per hour, AR = actual rate per hour. Positive = F, negative = A.

formulas.name: Labour Efficiency Variance
formulas.legend: SH = standard hours for actual output, AH worked = actual hours less idle hours. Positive = F, negative = A.

formulas.name: Idle Time Variance
formulas.legend: Always Adverse. Check: LCV = (SH × SR) − (AH paid × AR) = LRV + LEV + Idle TV.

insight.text: Rate variance tells about the price paid per hour; efficiency and idle time tell about hours used.

memory_trick.explanation: Always write Standard first, Actual second. A positive answer is Favourable, a negative one is Adverse. Use it for rate, efficiency and cost.

steps: Note AH paid, idle hrs, AH worked
Add up and tally with LCV
exam_tip: Rate variance uses hours paid; efficiency uses hours worked. Tally LRV + LEV + Idle TV with LCV to check.

doubt.question: Why is idle time variance always Adverse?
doubt.answer: Idle hours are paid for but give no output, so the cost is a loss against standard. Standard normally allows no idle time.

mistakes.wrong: Using hours worked for the rate variance
mistakes.right: LRV uses hours paid: AH paid × (SR − AR).

mistakes.wrong: Using actual hours paid in efficiency variance
mistakes.right: Use hours worked (paid hours less idle hours) in efficiency: SR × (SH − AH worked).

mistakes.wrong: Taking SH as standard hours for budgeted output
mistakes.right: SH is standard hours for the actual output produced.

Checker 1: Formula 3 legend / check (LCV = LRV + LEV + Idle TV): SR × Idle hours gives a positive number, but the note's rule is 'positive = F'. A student who adds it as positive will not get the tally right. Correct version: Idle TV = SR × Idle hours (A), and in the tally take it as a negative figure: LCV = LRV + LEV − (SR × Idle hours). You can also write Idle TV = SR × (0 − Idle hours) so it fits the 'Standard minus Actual' rule.

Checker 1: Doubt answer: 'Standard normally allows no idle time' should be more precise. Normal idle time is usually allowed for in the standard hours or rate. The idle time variance is about abnormal idle time hours that are paid but not worked. Suggested wording: 'Standards allow for normal idle time, so the variance is for abnormal idle hours paid but not worked.'
